stem: Best guess: a company changed its inventory method, applied it properly, and disclosed it. What does the auditor's report include?

choices.text: A qualified opinion for the change in principle
choices.explanation: A properly accounted-for change doesn't modify the opinion.

choices.text: An other-matter paragraph about the change
choices.explanation: The matter is in the statements, so it's emphasis of matter.

choices.text: An emphasis-of-matter paragraph on the disclosure
choices.explanation: Correct. AU-C 708 requires an emphasis-of-matter paragraph for a change in principle with a material effect.

choices.text: Nothing beyond the standard unmodified report
choices.explanation: A consistency paragraph is required.

explanation: AU-C 708 requires an emphasis-of-matter paragraph for a change in principle with a material effect.

stem: Which matter belongs in an **other-matter** paragraph?

choices.text: A significant subsequent event that is disclosed in the notes
choices.explanation: That's disclosed in the statements — emphasis of matter.

choices.text: A major catastrophe that is disclosed in the notes
choices.explanation: That's emphasis of matter.

choices.text: A properly applied change in accounting principle
choices.explanation: That's emphasis of matter.

choices.text: Prior-year statements audited by a predecessor, report not shown
choices.explanation: Correct. Other-matter paragraphs address matters not presented or disclosed in the statements.

explanation: Other-matter paragraphs address matters not presented or disclosed in the statements.

stem: Which best describes a critical audit matter under PCAOB AS 3101?

choices.text: A matter sent to the audit committee involving especially challenging judgment
choices.explanation: Correct. AS 3101 defines CAMs using all three elements.

choices.text: Any matter discussed with management during the audit
choices.explanation: CAMs come from matters communicated to the audit committee.

choices.text: Any matter that requires a qualified opinion on the statements
choices.explanation: CAMs don't substitute for modifications.

choices.text: Any control deficiency identified during the audit
choices.explanation: Deficiencies are communicated separately.

explanation: AS 3101 defines CAMs using all three elements.

stem: A company changed the estimated useful life of its equipment. What should the auditor's report include?

choices.text: An emphasis-of-matter paragraph
choices.explanation: Estimate changes don't affect consistency reporting.

choices.text: A qualified opinion
choices.explanation: A properly accounted-for estimate change isn't a departure.

choices.text: No additional paragraph
choices.explanation: Correct. Changes in accounting estimates don't require a consistency paragraph.

choices.text: An other-matter paragraph
choices.explanation: An estimate change doesn't call for an other-matter paragraph.

explanation: Changes in accounting estimates don't require a consistency paragraph.

stem: What statement accompanies an emphasis-of-matter paragraph?

choices.text: "Our opinion is qualified in this respect."
choices.explanation: Emphasis doesn't modify the opinion.

choices.text: "The statements do not present fairly in this respect."
choices.explanation: That's adverse.

choices.text: "We do not express an opinion on this matter."
choices.explanation: That's a disclaimer.

choices.text: "Our opinion is not modified with respect to this matter."
choices.explanation: Correct. AU-C 706: the paragraph indicates the opinion isn't modified with respect to the matter.

explanation: AU-C 706: the paragraph indicates the opinion isn't modified with respect to the matter.

stem: A company corrected a material misstatement in previously issued statements. What does the auditor's current report include?

choices.text: An emphasis-of-matter paragraph
choices.explanation: Correct. AU-C 708 requires an emphasis-of-matter paragraph for correction of a material misstatement in previously issued statements.

choices.text: Nothing beyond the standard report
choices.explanation: Correction of an error requires a paragraph.

choices.text: An adverse opinion on the prior year
choices.explanation: The corrected statements are fairly presented.

choices.text: A disclaimer on the restated year
choices.explanation: No scope limitation exists.

explanation: AU-C 708 requires an emphasis-of-matter paragraph for correction of a material misstatement in previously issued statements.

stem: For a nonissuer audit, when are key audit matters communicated in the auditor's report?

choices.text: Always, in every nonissuer audit report
choices.explanation: KAMs are reported only when the auditor is engaged to do so.

choices.text: Only when the opinion is qualified or adverse
choices.explanation: KAMs are unrelated to modification.

choices.text: When the auditor is engaged to communicate them
choices.explanation: Correct. AU-C 701 applies when the auditor is engaged (or required by law) to communicate KAMs.

choices.text: Never; KAMs apply only to issuer audits
choices.explanation: They can be reported if engaged.

explanation: AU-C 701 applies when the auditor is engaged (or required by law) to communicate KAMs.

stem: The annual report includes a CEO letter claiming revenue grew 20%; the audited statements show 5%. The CEO refuses to correct it. What should the auditor do?

choices.text: Nothing, because the auditor doesn't audit other information
choices.explanation: The auditor must consider material inconsistencies.

choices.text: Correct the CEO letter directly before the report is issued
choices.explanation: The auditor doesn't alter management's documents.

choices.text: Issue an adverse opinion on the audited financial statements
choices.explanation: The statements themselves aren't misstated.

choices.text: Describe the uncorrected misstatement in the Other Information section
choices.explanation: Correct. AU-C 720: if other information is materially misstated and not corrected, the auditor includes a statement in the Other Information section, or takes other action.

explanation: AU-C 720: if other information is materially misstated and not corrected, the auditor includes a statement in the Other Information section, or takes other action.

stem: Which of the following requires an emphasis-of-matter paragraph in a report on statements prepared under a special purpose framework?

choices.text: Alerting readers that the statements use a basis other than GAAP
choices.explanation: Correct. AU-C 800: an emphasis-of-matter paragraph alerts users to the special purpose framework.

choices.text: Stating the audit fee and the auditor's relationship to the client
choices.explanation: Fees aren't reported.

choices.text: Listing the members of the engagement team
choices.explanation: Team members aren't listed.

choices.text: Describing the auditor's sampling methods and results
choices.explanation: Sampling methods aren't described.

explanation: AU-C 800: an emphasis-of-matter paragraph alerts users to the special purpose framework.

stem: A CAM is identified for the valuation of goodwill. What must the auditor's report describe for it?

choices.text: Only that the matter exists and was discussed
choices.explanation: More is required.

choices.text: Why it is a CAM, how it was addressed, and the related accounts
choices.explanation: Correct. AS 3101: identify the CAM, describe why, how it was addressed, and refer to the relevant accounts or disclosures.

choices.text: A separate opinion on the goodwill balance
choices.explanation: No separate opinion is given.

choices.text: Management's impairment calculations in full
choices.explanation: Reproducing management's calculations isn't required.

explanation: AS 3101: identify the CAM, describe why, how it was addressed, and refer to the relevant accounts or disclosures.

stem: Can a key audit matter be used instead of a qualified opinion?

choices.text: Yes, if the matter is fully described in the KAM section
choices.explanation: KAMs aren't a substitute for modifications.

choices.text: No; KAMs never substitute for a modified opinion
choices.explanation: Correct. AU-C 701 and AS 3101 both prohibit using KAMs/CAMs in place of required modifications.

choices.text: Yes, but only in audits of nonissuers
choices.explanation: Substitution isn't permitted for any entity.

choices.text: Only when the client agrees to the substitution
choices.explanation: Client agreement doesn't change the rule.

explanation: AU-C 701 and AS 3101 both prohibit using KAMs/CAMs in place of required modifications.

stem: The auditor is engaged to report on supplementary information accompanying the audited statements. What opinion is given on it?

choices.text: A separate opinion on the fair presentation of the information
choices.explanation: It's reported on "in relation to" the statements.

choices.text: Whether it is fairly stated in relation to the statements
choices.explanation: Correct. AU-C 725: the auditor reports whether supplementary information is fairly stated in relation to the statements as a whole.

choices.text: No opinion is ever given on supplementary information
choices.explanation: An in-relation-to opinion is given.

choices.text: A review conclusion with limited assurance
choices.explanation: This is an audit engagement, not a review.

explanation: AU-C 725: the auditor reports whether supplementary information is fairly stated in relation to the statements as a whole.

stem: A company changed an accounting principle without reasonable justification. What is the effect on the report?

choices.text: An emphasis-of-matter paragraph only, with no modification
choices.explanation: An unjustified change is a GAAP departure.

choices.text: A qualified or adverse opinion, by pervasiveness
choices.explanation: Correct. A change not properly justified or accounted for is a departure from the framework → modified opinion.

choices.text: A disclaimer of opinion for the change
choices.explanation: It isn't a scope limitation.

choices.text: No effect if the change is disclosed
choices.explanation: The departure must be reported.

explanation: A change not properly justified or accounted for is a departure from the framework → modified opinion.
